newsitem.title: USA: IPO VIEW-Wall Street's dunk could dampen IPOs.
newsitem.headline: IPO VIEW-Wall Street's dunk could dampen IPOs.

text.p: Tagging along on Wall Street's rough-and-tumble ride, the new issues market may be bruised by recent stock market instability, industry experts said.

"When you have a volatile market on the downside, it's just hard to get investors interested in buying hot, volatile small-cap IPOs," said Linda Intini, vice president of Citibank Global Asset Management.

The Dow Jones Industrial average descended 247 points on Friday to close at 7695, retreating from its watermark 8,000 levels and lowering the curtain on a punishing week that saw an overall decline of 330 points in the index.
"The market just hasn't had a good feel to it in the last week and a half," Intini added.

Steve Zenker, a portfolio manager at McCabe Capital Managers, concurred that investor jitters could easily spill over into the initial public offerings arena, dampening reception to IPOs in the short term.

"There may be a sense of urgency starting to develop, especially if the (stock) market continues to look weak. I think people are going to push whatever (new issues) they can through the door as quickly as possible," he said.

Analysts stressed, though, that much would depend on Wall Street's performance in upcoming weeks, and that the last two weeks of August are typically slow in the new issues market, making it difficult to gauge trends during that time.

"Some of us try to avoid the last couple weeks in August just as a matter of course," said Richard Smith, managing syndicate director at Montgomery Securities. Noting that many of the market's major players will be vacationing in the latter part of the month he said, "It doesn't matter so much in terms of follow-ons, but in terms of IPOs you want to get as broad an exposure as possible."
When asked about the IPO market's general health, he said it was "not quite as ebullient" as earlier in the month.
Intini, of Citibank, did sound a bright note, however.

"We just had our first quarter in which the earnings growth for small-cap stocks was higher than it was for large-cap stocks, and that hasn't happened since the mid-1994," she said. Most IPOs fit into the small-capitalization catagory.
And if this week's batch of IPOs represents light, summer fare, September and October should produce some deals for investors to sink their teeth into.

"The majority of the people I've talked to have their most crowded new issues calendar for September and October than in the last few years," said Michael Essex, syndicate manager at McDonald Securities. "There's going to be a lot of product pushing through in the Fall," he added.

Among the week's larger offerings is Positron Fiber System Corp, a $50 million deal by underwriters Robertson Stephens & Co. The company, which designs broadband access network systems, is offering five million shares in a pricing range of $9.00 to $11.00.

Also offering five million shares, in a $14.00 to $16.00 range, is CTB International Corp, by underwriters Donaldson, Lufkin & Jenrette Securities Corp. The company manufactures automated feeding and ventilation systems for poultry and hogs.
"We thought Kendle International was attractive," said Robert Natale, director of equity research at Standard and Poor's Corp.
Kendle, which is offering 3.6 million shares for between $12.00 and $14.00, specializes in contract research for the approval of drugs.

"It's not an emerging technology, but it's an emerging outsourcing business," Natale said, adding the company could potentially take over monitoring of drug trials now under the federal government's domain, and that it had a strong backlog.
